| [QUESTION-120](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md) v4 | When the record meets a random linear map that keeps what a later stage needs, in random features for kernels, the compressed-sensing bound on superposition, and the expand-and-threshold codes of sparse distributed memory and the fly, is it one concentration-of-measure fact applied to different families, and does each threshold count the same thing? | Filed when a survey of the record found random projections in three places and the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma in none. The three uses carry three thresholds: ε⁻² log n for distances, k log(n/k) for sparse recovery, and 2N = n for random-features regression. The question is whether these are one union bound over different families or different phenomena that share a tool. Six anchor works are now read. They show the distance and sparse-recovery thresholds share a sufficiency proof, but not a necessity proof, and give nothing that reaches the other two uses. For SDM and the fly, the record's SDM recall account and its LSH account offer candidate thresholds of a different shape. | Open |
| [QUESTION-123](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-123.md) | How should an organization's demands be tracked across differentiation, branching, merging and changes of organizational identity, when no one-to-one correspondence between earlier and later demands exists? | A39's, from the exchange of 2026-10-17: "How should demands be tracked across differentiation, branching, merging, and changes of organizational identity?" [CLAIM-361](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-361.md) judges relief against a fixed reference set of demands under an explicit correspondence between earlier and later demands. When the processes that bear the demands split or merge, that correspondence may not be a bijection, and [CLAIM-287](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md) says the continuity it would follow can branch and is not an identity relation. An answer says what structure the correspondence has, and how relief is judged through it. | Open |
| [QUESTION-130](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-130.md) | Does transport of evaluative representations between contexts, with the evaluated situation held fixed, admit a connection fixed by independently established relations rather than chosen, and is its holonomy around a loop of contexts ever nontrivial? | The owner's, U19 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, self-hedged: "this might be a stretch, but given our framework already leverages fields and flows, are we perhaps moving towards a gauge theoretic account of something here?" A19 separated representational gauge freedom, which the record holds ([CLAIM-148](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-148.md)), from a connection between contexts and from nontrivial curvature, and kept the last speculative. The first objection is the record's own: it rejected [LIT-038](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-038.md), whose path-dependent transport across a network of causal models comes from arbitrary maps ([NOTE-050](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-050.md)). The first target is flat holonomy. An answer derives transport from shared commitments, causal effects or roles in a finite model and reports whether a loop's holonomy is trivial. | Open |
